parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: A cylindrical metal wire of length $2.4\text{ m}$ and cross-sectional area $8.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$ has a resistance of $0.33\Omega$. There is a current in the wire of $4.7\text{ A}$.
parts.text: Determine the resistivity of the metal from which the wire is made.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the charge that passes through the wire in a time of $5.0$ minutes.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The free electrons (charge carriers) in the wire have an average drift speed of $0.16\text{ mm s}^{-1}$.

Determine the number density of charge carriers in the metal.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The wire in (b) may be considered to be a fixed resistor. It is connected in series with a thermistor to a battery that has negligible internal resistance.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, without calculation, how the power dissipated in the wire changes as the temperature of the thermistor is increased.
